findings.title: Password reset accepts an expired reset_token
findings.explanation: consumeToken in src/auth/reset.js no longer compares record.expires_at against Date.now(), so any token ever issued keeps working. The expiry constant RESET_TTL_MS is now unused.
findings.next_action: Restore the expiry comparison in consumeToken before the password write, and re-enable test/reset.test.js:"rejects an expired token".

evidence.summary: npm run test: 1 failing - "rejects an expired token" expected 400, received 200.
consumeToken is reached from the unauthenticated POST /auth/reset/confirm route in src/server/routes.js:88.
File rule glob src/auth/** matched; RESET_TTL_MS became unreferenced in this diff.

findings.title: Rate limit window widened from 60s to 900s
findings.suppressed_reason: severity medium is below min_severity high
findings.explanation: WINDOW_MS changed from 60_000 to 900_000, which also loosens the login throttle, not only the reset throttle this diff targets.
findings.next_action: Confirm the login throttle is meant to change too, or give the reset flow its own window.

insufficient.summary: sendResetMail in src/auth/mailer.js logs its whole payload, but the logger sink is configured outside this repository.
missing_evidence: whether the payload still contains reset_token at that point

rules.text: Breaks an existing caller or public API contract.
Removes or weakens an authentication, permission or validation check.
Secrets, personal data or unfiltered records reach logs, responses or other tenants.
Changes existing behaviour outside the apparent purpose of the diff.
Reset tokens must be single use and expire within 15 minutes.
